children: New Delhi, Oct. 17 -- Snabbit's losses widened nearly 30-fold to Rs.167.75 crore in fiscal year 2026 (FY26) from Rs.5.70 crore in FY25, as the instant house-help startup ramped up spending on workers and marketing to expand its business.

Revenue from operations rose to Rs.12.25 crore in the year ended 31 March 2026 from Rs.26.35 lakh a year earlier, according to financial statements of Maestroedge Solutions Pvt. Ltd, which operates Snabbit.

Speaking on LinkedIn about the losses, the startup's founder and chief executive Aayush Agarwal said that building a business from "scratch" requires significant investment, even when spending far exceeds revenue.
He said the company "deliberately" invested in customer adoption, workforce training, technology, infrastructure and geographic expansion, adding that it would make the same investments again.

"But what an annual P&L doesn't tell you is that at the beginning of FY26, we were losing approximately Rs.1,500 per job. Last month, that number was below Rs.200. And it continues to improve," he noted.
Agarwal also highlighted the scale of job creation as Snabbit expanded its operations and strengthened its presence across markets.

"FY26 was our first full year of operations. We started the year at 500 jobs a day and exited at 35,000. That's 70x growth in 12 months. Along the way, we acquired nearly a million customers, onboarded 20,000+ Experts, and built the infrastructure to create an entirely new consumer category," he added.

"We're not building a business that depends on spending more to grow more. We're building one where every additional layer of scale makes the underlying economics stronger. The losses of FY26 reflect what it took to create this category. The numbers of FY27 reflect what that investment is beginning to deliver," he wrote in the social media post.

Snabbit's total expenses rose to Rs.194.76 crore in FY26 from Rs.6.81 crore a year earlier, highlighting its efforts to capture market share in the instant home-help segment, where it competes with established player Urban Company.

Costs relating to professionals were Snabbit's largest expense at Rs.63.07 crore, followed by marketing at Rs.48.69 crore, employee expenses at Rs.46.02 crore and service fulfilment expenses at Rs.23.83 crore.
Revenue included Rs.10.82 crore from platform services and Rs.1.42 crore from uniform sales. Snabbit reports revenue after deducting discounts it pays for to lower customers' bills.
Other income, mainly interest on bank deposits, contributed Rs.14.77 crore, taking total income to Rs.27.01 crore.
Agarwal holds a Post Graduate Diploma in Management (PGDM) in Finance from Institute of Management Technology, Ghaziabad.

He previously worked as a finance manager at White Owl before joining Zepto in 2022 as senior manager of finance. He was later elevated to the position of vice president and chief of staff at the quick-commerce company.

In 2024, Agarwal founded Snabbit, an on-demand home services platform that provides verified and trained domestic help at customers' doorsteps in approximately 10 minutes, with services starting at Rs.99 per hour.

title: Meet Aayush Agarwal: Snabbit boss explains why 'house help' firm suffered Rs.168 cr loss on Rs.12 cr revenue in FY26
